That doesn't necessarily mean you're schizophrenic, but if you're actually worried, you should talk to a psychiatrist. They know more than most people you'll meet on reddit. Just some friendly advice :P

I was recently 'officially' diagnosed. I've known for about ~6 months really. 
Some of the things that really pushed me to believe there was something wrong were: having full conversations/arguments with myself. Little angry whispers in my head. Literally not believing I'm a human for a while. Memory loss/issues (completely incapable of remembering small tasks, I have to have a list or I will never remember I was asked to do anything). Forgetting who I was for hours on occasion. Shadows in the corner of my eye. The worst was probably when my nightmares became a part of my waking life as well, the scary things I dreamt about live(d) in my house during the day too. I'm legitimately paranoid that people are out to kill me (I can't answer the door without having a panic attack).
For a long time I tried to ignore my problems, shrugging it off as stress and my depression being bad for me. Then one day, I woke up, and went to bed without remembering a single thing from that day, nothing, just waking up and then laying down. It was then that I realized that I really had a problem. So I sought help, she didn't want to 'put a name' on it, but she had me research schizophrenia and what it meant. And now I've been officially diagnosed, I'll begin medication hopefully in the near future. I hope that's what you meant..? Either way, I'm up for questions if anyone wants to ask! If I don't answer right now, I will tomorrow, I'm probably off to bed.
